content:
Developers can now install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7, just one week after the release of beta 6. Here are the details.

Apple releases macOS 27 beta 7

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 after a three-week hiatus in beta releases, introducing redesigned traffic light window controls. macOS 27 beta 6 no longer uses flat red, yellow, and green circular buttons, but instead adds a Liquid Glass (actually quite similar to Aqua) effect to the minimize, maximize, and close buttons.

Aside from this, macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 did not introduce any other user-facing new features or improvements, suggesting Apple may be using the final few betas to fix bugs and improve performance and security in preparation for the official launch.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces an all-new Siri app and a redesigned Siri AI. The system also features an AI-powered new version of the Shortcuts app that can create shortcuts based on natural language instructions, as well as a Safari extension builder that generates content based on prompts.

In addition, macOS 27 Golden Gate launches new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while returning window and app corners to a fixed radius. This reverses a change made in macOS 26, which adjusted the corner radius based on the contents of each window or app's menu bar.

macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7 has build number 26A5421a. We are examining the new beta closely and will report on the changes later.

How to install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General ⇾ Software Update
  • Click the "i" icon next to "Beta Updates"
  • Select "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta" from the dropdown menu in the top right corner
  • Click "Done"

Have you noticed any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments section.
